rounds.text: Solara Active Pharma Sciences Ltd presents a compelling turnaround story underpinned by accelerating top-line momentum and robust cash generation, with trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth reaching 15% [E16] and three-year compounded profit growth hitting 25% [E17]. Operational efficiency is visibly improving, highlighted by a dramatic 20 percentage point expansion in operating margins to 13% from -7% three years prior [E25]. This operational recovery directly translates into strong financial health, evidenced by Mar 2026 operating cash flow of Rs 153 Cr—representing 83% of operating profit—and free cash flow of Rs 101 Cr [E30, E31], while total borrowings decreased from Rs 796 Cr to Rs 687 Cr [E35]. Insider and market confidence is further reinforced by promoters increasing their stake by 4.74 percentage points to 41.93% [E37], alongside domestic institutions expanding their holdings [E39]. Technically and macroeconomically, the stock displays exceptional relative strength with a score of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E44], trading above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E43], while benefiting from a strong healthcare sector tailwind score of +0.85 to +0.83 [E65, E67]. conceded: [E10], [E18], [E55].

The stock trades at an exorbitant trailing P/E of 753x and an EV/EBITDA of 19.43x against a sector benchmark of 17.13x, while offering a dividend yield of 0.00% [E1, E4, E11]. Compounded sales growth over five and three years stands at -3% and -2% respectively, and compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months collapsed by -83% [E14, E15, E18]. Profitability metrics remain deeply troubled, highlighted by a 5-year median return on equity of -7%, a 3-year median ROE of -12%, and a low ROCE of 4.9% [E12, E22, E23]. Balance sheet and capital structure strains are evident through a current ratio of 0.96x where current liabilities exceed current assets, a low interest coverage ratio, and a concerning 37.1% pledge of promoter holdings [E34, E52, E55]. Institutional confidence is fading as foreign institutions reduced their stake from 17.86% to 11.52%, resulting in negative institutional money flow and decelerating earnings growth [E38, E40, E61]. This operational turnaround directly translates into hard cash generation rather than paper earnings, with operating cash flow reaching Rs 153 Cr and free cash flow hitting Rs 101 Cr in March 2026 [E30, E31]. Crucially, insiders are putting their capital behind this turnaround rather than fleeing, as promoter ownership increased significantly from 37.19% to 41.93% [E37]. Finally, the market is beginning to validate this momentum, with the stock trading firmly above its 50-day and 200-day moving averages alongside a stellar relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E43, E44].

While the bull highlights recent sales growth [E16], this fails to offset a five-year compounded sales decline of -3% [E14, E53], and the cited margin expansion [E25] is already reversing with a quarterly drop from 18% to 16% [E26] amid an inconsistent trend [E27, E28].
